sources.title: PyTorch/XLA pinned Pallas bridge and JAX import guard
sources.date_basis: GitHub commit committer date for the pinned snapshot; not a file modification date
supports: The bridge traces positional Torch tensors as storage-free shape and dtype objects.
The bridge sends the Torch tensors and extracted custom-call configuration to the XLA call.
The output callback returns a list of shape and dtype pairs.
The guard initializes the PyTorch/XLA client before JAX import.
The bridge rejects enabled XLA_USE_BF16.
limitations: Tensor containers and tensor keyword arguments lack positional operand handling.
The extractor does not preserve arbitrary surrounding JAX operations.
This source does not qualify the backend functionalization wrapper.

sources.title: JAX 0.7.1 BlockSpec squeezed axes
sources.date_basis: GitHub tag commit committer date for jax-v0.7.1; not a file modification date
supports: None maps to a squeezed axis.
The Ref shape omits squeezed axes.
The complete block shape gives a squeezed axis size one.
limitations: A squeezed Ref axis does not remove that axis from Mosaic block validation.
This inspection does not compile the grouped layout.

sources.title: JAX 0.7.1 Mosaic block, gather, and dot lowering
sources.date_basis: GitHub tag commit committer date for jax-v0.7.1; main comparison has its own snapshot date
supports: The final two block dimensions must meet 8/128 divisibility or cover their complete array dimensions.
HIGHEST dot precision lowers to the FP32 contraction attribute.
The pinned source rejects HIGH dot precision.
The pinned source supports limited gather patterns.
Observed main supports an additional HIGH lowering and still contains the divisibility rule.
limitations: The leading group layout passes one source rule, not all compiler constraints.
Current main behavior does not establish compatibility with JAX 0.7.1.
Narrow-type slices and decode vector layouts require actual compilation.

sources.title: JAX 0.7.1 TPU matmul example
sources.date_basis: GitHub tag commit committer date for jax-v0.7.1
supports: The example uses tile operands, accumulator scratch storage, and sequential K traversal.
Floating-point inputs use an FP32 accumulator.
The source contains integer accumulator branches.
limitations: The example does not decode NF4 or implement bitsandbytes storage.
The example does not validate the proposed tile sizes for this workload.

sources.title: Current JAX TPU kernel restrictions
sources.date_basis: The page supplies no publication date; accessed date is separate
supports: The guide describes HBM input storage and VMEM or SMEM kernel references.
The guide states the final-dimension block restriction.
The guide warns that FP32 dot inputs need explicit FP32 precision.
The guide describes narrower-type slicing restrictions.
limitations: Rolling documentation is not version-specific evidence for JAX 0.7.1.
The inspected main source snapshot is a separate record.

sources.title: Current JAX TPU matmul and fused transpose guide
sources.date_basis: No page publication date is displayed; source notebook last commit is recorded separately
supports: The guide uses dot_general for a fused right operand transpose.
The guide explains tile size, repeated input reads, pipeline overhead, and VMEM limits.
Some guide timings exclude operand relayout costs.
limitations: Dense matmul examples do not prove NF4 performance.
Kernel-only timings do not measure canonical packed preparation.
Current notebook syntax cannot be assumed valid in JAX 0.7.1.

sources.title: PyTorch/XLA pinned quantized TPU matmul kernel
sources.date_basis: GitHub commit committer date for the pinned snapshot
supports: The kernel provides tiled integer matmul, scales, scratch storage, and selected block size examples.
The inspected entry rejects quant_block_size.
The wrapper can select an XLA quantized path when tuned sizes are unavailable.
limitations: The inspected kernel does not implement the NF4 codebook or high-nibble-first bitsandbytes format.
Its path selection cannot prove that the proposed NF4 call executed Pallas.

sources.title: PyTorch/XLA pinned memory information and synchronization
sources.date_basis: GitHub commit committer date for the pinned snapshot
supports: The native binding returns bytes_used, bytes_limit, and peak_bytes_used.
The wrapper has no interval peak reset argument.
wait_device_ops waits for asynchronous operations.
mark_step calls torch_xla.sync.
limitations: The source does not define these values as kernel VMEM measurements.
A synchronization wait does not itself submit a pending lazy graph.
The target interval and process-scope peak need separate qualification.
The device client peak scope requires runtime verification.

sources.title: OpenXLA HLO and Mosaic dump documentation
sources.date_basis: Displayed Last updated date, not initial publication date
supports: The guide describes HLO dumps and identifies before/after optimization and buffer assignment records.
The guide gives the xla_mosaic_dump_to flag for Mosaic computations.
limitations: Flag support remains unverified for libtpu 0.0.21.
An outer custom call can conceal internal storage.
Compiler records are not allocator peak measurements.

sources.title: Pinned bitsandbytes MatMul4Bit backward
sources.date_basis: GitHub commit committer date for the pinned snapshot
supports: Forward invokes the bitsandbytes gemm_4bit operator.
Activation backward calls dequantize_4bit before torch.matmul.
Bias backward uses an upstream reduction.
limitations: A Pallas forward memory result does not prove training memory reduction.
Public backward still requires direct tests.

sources.title: Qwix NF4 numerics, QLoRA example, and contributed TPU matmul
sources.date_basis: GitHub main commit committer date for the observed snapshot
supports: Qwix includes NF4 conversion and a JAX/Flax QLoRA example.
The numerics source excludes NF4 from decoding after the dot operation.
The contributed TPU matmul applies scales after a low-precision dot.
The inspected contributed kernel has no NF4 codebook decode.
limitations: QArray values do not establish bitsandbytes packed bytes or QuantState compatibility.
This related implementation does not qualify this backend M5.
No Qwix runtime or kernel test occurred.

sources.title: Tokamax kernel selection, tuning architecture, and runtime requirements
sources.date_basis: GitHub main commit committer date for the observed snapshot
supports: Tokamax supports explicit implementation selection and serialized tuning results.
The operation classes separate the reference implementation from accelerator implementations.
The observed main package requires JAX and jaxlib 0.11.0 or later.
limitations: Current requirements conflict with qualified JAX/jaxlib 0.7.1.
Inspected sources do not establish a drop-in bitsandbytes NF4 operator.
No dependency installation or autotuning occurred.
